newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaha to form water purifier venture.
newsitem.headline: Yamaha to form water purifier venture.

text.p: Yamaha Motor Co Ltd said on Thursday it would set up a new company next month in Jakarta, Indonesia, to produce and sell water purifiers.

The new company, named P.T. Yamaha Motor Nuansa Indonesia (YMNI), will be owned 70 percent by IIC Ltd, a Japanese maker of water purifiers and motorcycle components, 20 percent by Yamaha and 10 percent by P.T. Yamaha Indonesia Motor Manufacturing (YIMM).
Yamaha now produces water purifiers in Indonesia at YIMM for sales through Yamaha Motor Kencana Indonesia (YMKI).
The new company will take over the production and sales of water purifiers from YIMM and YMKI. YIMM and YMKI will concentrate on production and sales of motorcycles.
YMNI hopes to achieve annual sales of 400 million yen, or $3.6 million, in the first year to January 1998, and 1.2 billion yen, or $10.9 million, in annual sales after five years.
In the whole of Indonesia, 16 percent of people use tap water, with the rest relying on well water. The rate of tap water use in the capital Jakarta is 40 percent, a Yamaha spokesman said.
